problem:
Given the polynomial $P(x)=(x+4)(3-x)(1-x),$ find the solution of $P(x)>0.$

$x\in ($
{{field-1}}$,\,1)⋃($
{{field-2}}$,$
{{field-3}}$)$
worked_solution:
To solve the inequality $P(x)>0,$ we need to find the values of $x$ for which the curve $y=P(x)$ lies above the $x$-axis.

The roots of the polynomial $P(x)=(x+4)(3-x)(1-x)$ are $x=-4,\,x=3,$ and $x=1,$ which are all simple roots.

Also, $P(x)$ is a cubic polynomial with a positive leading coefficient. So, we can graph the curve as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14007649/assets/691c37edf48a5d7807f7c43d73b0ac014358632a1957e3016f953af6f47c8f36.png)

Since we are interested in solving $P(x)>0,$ we look for the part of the curve that is above the $x$-axis. 

Based on the graph, the solution is $x\in (-4,1)⋃(3,\infty ).$
